provenance.note: `Ipex` takes a whole `SignifyClient`, so the real client is driven with `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a recorder that signs its answers as a KERIA agent would. The sender's habitat is derived by the same route the pinned `test/app/test-utils.ts` derives its mock, at the reference's production Argon2 cost, so every signature in a recorded body is real. Each message is built by the reference's own Roadmap 6.3 builder before being submitted, so every recorded `exn` is one `fixtures/acdc-ipex/v1.json` has already proven byte-exact. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode is the pinned tests' own and has never protected anything.

notes.attachment: `submitApply` and `submitAgree` take **no** `atc` parameter and write none, although their own builders return an attachment as the third element of the tuple — so two of the five submitters discard a value the builder produced
notes.recipients: every submitter takes a `recp: string[]` and copies it into the body as `rec`; nothing compares it with the recipient the message itself names in `rp` and `a.i`
notes.path: each path interpolates the sender's alias raw and appends a route segment the method chooses, so the route and the resource can only agree by the caller picking the matching method

pinned_confirmations.note: the pinned `credentialing.test.ts` calls all five submitters across its three IPEX cases and asserts each one's full URL, which is the whole of what it checks about them — no body is asserted anywhere. `clienting.test.ts` asserts the type of five other endpoint accessors and **not** this one, which is recorded as a scan rather than claimed. Every real call site in the pinned tree, unit and integration alike, passes exactly one recipient and it is the one the message itself addresses; nothing in the reference compares the two.

two_submitters_discard_their_own_attachm.note: `Ipex.apply` and `Ipex.agree` each return an attachment as the third element of their tuple, and `submitApply` and `submitAgree` take no `atc` parameter and write no `atc` field — so the value is built and dropped. It is always the empty string, because neither route embeds anything, so nothing is actually lost; the asymmetry is in the API rather than in the bytes.
two_submitters_discard_their_own_attachm.rust_decision: reproduced exactly: the route decides whether the body carries `atc`, so an apply and an agree write three fields and the other three write four. A property asserts an apply's and an agree's attachment is always empty, which is what makes the omission lossless.

the_route_and_the_resource_agree_only_by.note: each submitter appends its own route segment and accepts any `exn`, so posting a grant through `submitApply` addresses `/ipex/apply` with a message whose own `r` says `/ipex/grant` — and posting an apply through `submitGrant` adds an `atc` the message never had. Nothing checks either.
the_route_and_the_resource_agree_only_by.rust_decision: unrepresentable: there is one `submit`, and the path segment is read from the message's own route, so the resource and the `r` field cannot disagree.

detail.note: read from the pinned source text rather than executed, because most call sites are integration tests needing a live KERIA; every one passes a single-element list

nothing_compares_the_recipients_with_the.note: the recipient list is copied into the body as `rec` and is never compared with the `rp` and `a.i` the message itself carries, so a grant addressed to one identifier can be handed to the agent for delivery to another. Every call site in the pinned tree passes exactly one recipient and it is the addressee, so the reference has no evidence either way about fanning out.
nothing_compares_the_recipients_with_the.rust_decision: the list is kept as upstream and **not** narrowed to the addressee, because a multisig sender plausibly needs more than one and the pinned tree proves nothing either way; the method documents that it does not check. What is refused is an **empty** list, which asks the agent to deliver to nobody.

an_empty_recipient_list_is_sent.note: `recp: []` reaches the wire as `"rec":[]`, a submission the agent is asked to deliver to no one; the reference neither refuses it nor reports it
an_empty_recipient_list_is_sent.rust_decision: a typed refusal before anything is sent

the_alias_is_not_encoded.note: all five paths interpolate the sender's alias raw, so an alias holding a slash addresses a different identifier's IPEX resource — and Roadmap 3.10 signs `@path`, so it changes what the signature covers
the_alias_is_not_encoded.rust_decision: refused by construction: Roadmap 5.3's `ResourcePath` encodes the alias exactly once

the_answer_is_cast_rather_than_decoded.note: every submitter returns `response.json()` cast to `ExchangeOperation`, so whatever the agent sends is read as an operation
the_answer_is_cast_rather_than_decoded.rust_decision: decoded rather than cast, as Roadmap 6.8, 6.10, and 6.11 decided
